Officers from the Future City police, along with police, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and Transport Department officials conducting an inspection of the accident site in Shamshabad. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement

Seven people were killed in two separate road accidents on NH-44 and the Outer Ring Road (ORR) on the outskirts of Hyderabad in the early hours of Saturday (September 19). While four members of a family returning after Ganesh immersion died near Shamshabad, three workers were killed after a truck rammed their stationary goods vehicle near Shamirpet.
The first accident occurred sometime between 2.30 a.m. and 3 a.m. on NH-44 at Palamakula village, near a petrol station in Shamshabad.

Kethavath Limbya, 54, his wife Kethavath Jamuna, 45, Katravath Mansingh, 48, and Kethavath Vasram, 45, were killed after the Innova in which they were travelling went out of control and crashed into a bridge, police said.

The family was travelling from their native Mettugadda Thanda in Nawabpet mandal of Mahabubnagar district towards Shamshabad after attending Ganesh immersion. The driver, Sabavath Ashok, suffered serious injuries and was shifted to a private hospital in Shamshabad.
Future City Traffic DCP Shivam Upadhyaya later conducted a joint inspection of the accident site along with police, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and Transport Department officials.
Police said the road was found to be in good condition during the inspection and no cement blocks were present at the accident spot. A ‘Go Slow’ signboard was also found in place.

Based on the preliminary inspection, police suspect that the Innova was being driven at high speed before the driver lost control and hit the bridge structure. Further investigation is under way to establish the exact circumstances.
Hours earlier, three workers were killed after a Tata truck rammed into their stationary Ashok Leyland goods vehicle on the ORR near Shamirpet while they were trying to replace a flat tyre.
The victims, Ismail Hussain, 26, Rinku and Ibrahim, were travelling with Ashok and Bhim Shah from Chegunta towards Keesara in a vehicle carrying scrap.

After passing ORR Exit No. 6 at Shamirpet and crossing a foot-over bridge, the vehicle had a puncture on its rear right tyre. The vehicle was subsequently parked in the emergency lane on the left side of the ORR.

Police said Rinku and Ibrahim were attempting to remove the punctured tyre using a jack rod, while Ismail was underneath the vehicle holding a torch. Ashok and Bhim Shah had gone to collect stones to place beneath the vehicle for support.
It was then that a Tata truck allegedly being driven rashly rammed the stationary vehicle from behind.

Rinku and Ismail suffered severe injuries and died on the spot. Ibrahim was shifted to a hospital but died while undergoing treatment. According to the complaint, Bhim Shah told police that he had seen the truck driver, who identified himself as Nagaraju, a resident of Miyapur. The driver allegedly fled the scene following the collision.
Shamirpet police registered a case based on a complaint lodged by Ismail’s brother Mohd. Hussain and launched an investigation.
